question: Should Telegram suppress any system-marked notices at the adapter layer, and if so which typed payloads must remain deliverable?
rationale: Current docs and merged compaction-delivery history say configured compaction notices are user-facing, while the PR proposes a broad channel policy change without a typed boundary or proof.

options.title: Preserve configured notices and narrow suppression
options.body: Revise the PR so Telegram suppresses only a typed unwanted internal notice class while `notifyUser`, command replies, and visible status messages continue to deliver.

options.title: Accept broad Telegram suppression
options.body: Intentionally change the Telegram delivery contract, update docs/tests/config expectations, and provide upgrade-facing proof that users will not lose required feedback.

options.title: Close in favor of existing sanitizer paths
options.body: Treat the current sanitizer and related delivery-contract work as the supported direction unless a concrete Telegram-only leak report needs a narrower patch.

recommendation.title: Preserve configured notices and narrow suppression
recommendation.body: Revise the PR so Telegram suppresses only a typed unwanted internal notice class while `notifyUser`, command replies, and visible status messages continue to deliver.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged repair that most directly defines the current compaction notice delivery behavior affected by this PR.
